about: PROPOSAL-092. What each shape number of each template looks like, what changed from the number before it, and the paths the flows create each document at. The CURRENT number is not stored here: it is the number on the template's own `<!-- dflow-shape: ... -->` line. Paths are relative to dflow/specs/, and `*` matches within one path segment.

changes.migration: _index.md, Sync to BC layer in the head comment: where it says the sync continues the Step 8.3 / Step 5.3 sync mechanism, say instead that for a feature that carries phase-specs /dflow:finish-feature is the only step that writes the feature's changes into the bounded context, and until then they are in the Current BR Snapshot and the phase-specs. Keep the rest of the comment as it is, including anything the project added, and show the developer the old and new sentence before writing; until they answer, change nothing.

analysis.md, column Role-specific actions: a doc that already has this column keeps its values; bring them to one line per role and action. When you add this column, put it just before Evidence, give a row that is the template's placeholder the template's placeholder cell, and fill the other rows from what the project has already established: differences recorded elsewhere - after a role in Roles, or in a column the project added for them - move into this column, one line per role and action; a function more than one role reaches whose roles the project has already found able to do the same there gets `—`; every other row stays empty, which records that nobody has checked it yet - do not write `{TBD}`.

analysis.md, comments at the top of the document: replace the Referring to a rule comment with the template's. The Placement and Entry ids comments changed too; for those two, keeping yours is a valid answer.

analysis.md, Lifecycles comment: replace this section's comment with the template's. A value you left out of a state table to get a diagram goes back in, with the line after the tables that says where the list of values was taken from; dflow render now lists a value no transition has under the diagram instead of drawing it. If you do not know which values were left out, rebuild the list from where it was taken - the code or the data query - and do not guess. A state written `[*]` that is a stored value gets a name instead. Other lifecycles stay valid as they are: when you next change one, a create or delete step written below its table becomes a row with `[*]` in From or To, and the table gets that line.
analysis.md, Function / Role Index comment: replace this section's comment with the template's.

analysis.md, Cross-Context Flows comment: add the template's sentence about a part whose bounded context nobody has decided to this section's comment, and keep the rest of it as it is, including anything the project added or translated; show the developer the sentence before writing it, and until they answer, change nothing. Existing flows stay as they are: the rule applies the next time a change writes that flow.

analysis.md, Lifecycles comment: add to this section's comment the template's sentences about a value the code tests for but nothing it reads writes, and the template's addition to the values that get a short name (a value made only of symbols, such as `*`); keep the rest of the comment as it is, including anything the project added or translated, and show the developer the sentences before writing them. Where a State cell holds a value made only of symbols, give it a short name no other value of that field uses, in the state table and in the From and To cells that hold it; say in the line after the tables what the name stands for, keeping that line's existing evidence; leave the stored value as it is wherever a rule, a scenario or data evidence quotes it, and leave the `[*]` create and remove marker as it is. Show the developer each rename before writing it, and until they answer, change neither the comment nor any name. Leave the transitions as they are: the new sentences apply the next time a change writes that lifecycle.
behavior.md, Purpose note: replace the old Purpose with the template's; the old one says this file records what the system does now.

behavior.md, Maintenance in the head note: where it says the file is updated during Step 8.3, say instead that /dflow:finish-feature Step 3 updates it for a feature that carries phase-specs, and /dflow:modify-existing for a lightweight change on a host of its own. Keep the rest of the note as it is, including anything the project added, and show the developer the old and new sentence before writing; until they answer, change nothing.

context-map.md, External Systems: add the section from the current template, after Relationships. For each external system this file records elsewhere - as a row of the tables above, as one end of a Relationships row, or in Integration Notes - write a row there for each way it exchanges data, and carry every value those places held into it: the contexts that use it, and how, into Used By; any other value (a Subdomain Type, an owner, a code area, a published language, an ACL location, event names, notes) into the matching cell or Notes, or into an Integration Notes line that names the external system and the context it belongs to. Do not fill a cell by inference: write `—` for a value the old record does not give, and when it does not say which data moves by which mechanism or when, keep what it says in one row; ask the developer, and record what they leave unanswered in Open Questions. If the file already has an External Systems section, match each of its columns to the template's by meaning, not by position, and move a column the template has no place for into Notes. Show the developer the new rows and where each old value went before you remove or rewrite anything; until they answer, remove and rewrite nothing. When it is unclear whether an entry is an external system or one of this system's contexts, ask the developer. When the file records none, add the table header only.

context-map.md, Undecided Neighbors: add the section from the current template, after External Systems. A part of this system that this file records in the Context List or at one end of a Relationships row, but whose bounded context nobody has decided - a name carrying a note such as "not captured" or "boundary to be confirmed", say - may be a neighbor: list those names to the developer and ask which ones are. For each one they confirm, write one row there under one working name and carry every value its old rows held into Exchanges, Code Area or Notes, writing `—` for a value the old record does not give; show the developer the new rows and where each old value went, and remove the old rows only after they answer - until then, remove and rewrite nothing. Change only this file: other documents keep the names they use, so list those names in the row's Notes ("also called …"). A name the developer says is a bounded context stays where it is. When there is no such name, the section holds only its table header.
